bmt-2015-power-01a.prompt: The *Fano plane* has $7$ points and $7$ lines (see figure): the points are the three vertices of a triangle, the midpoints of its three sides, and the center; the lines are the three sides (each containing a vertex, a midpoint, and a vertex), the three medians (each through a vertex, the center, and the opposite midpoint), and the circle through the three midpoints. bmt-2015-power-04.prompt: A projective plane satisfies: (a) any two distinct points are on a unique line; (b) any two distinct lines meet in a unique point; (c) there are four points, no three on a line. A *degenerate* projective plane is a set of points and lines with an incidence relation satisfying (a) and (b) but not (c): among any four points, at least three are collinear. (The empty plane satisfies (a) and (b) vacuously.) Prove that a nonempty degenerate projective plane is one of three types: (i) there is a line and no points, or there is a point and no lines; (ii) there is a line $\ell$ incident to all points, and a point $p$ such that every other line (if any) is incident to just the point $p$; (iii) there is a line $\ell$ incident to all points except one point $p$, and every other line (if any) is incident to just $p$ and one point of $\ell$.
bmt-2015-power-04.answer: Case analysis: all points on one line (type ii), or a line $\ell$ with at least $3$ points and exactly one point $p$ off it (type iii), or three non-collinear points with exactly their three joining lines (type iii).
